quotes.text: Learn how to use Stripe subscriptions and invoices with third party payment processors.
This article has multiple variants. Fetch one of the following URLs to view specific content for your use case:

old_evidence.text: Create and manage [charge automatically](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/collection-method.md#automatic-charging-versus-manual-payments) subscriptions with off-Stripe payments using [custom payment methods](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-methods/custom-payment-methods.md) that reference off-Stripe payment methods

You must [report a payment](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-records.md#report-a-new-payment) within 23 hours of creating the subscription, or the subscription transitions to `incomplete_expired` and you need to recreate it.
When payment on the third party processor is successful, mark the corresponding invoice as `paid_out_of_band`.

findings: The 2026-11-07 base-URL capture is a 14-line navigation index with exactly two named variant links: own processor and out-of-band invoices (new raw:5-14). It establishes that these routes exist in this capture, but no current API version, integration support, processor eligibility, payment state, refund process, retry rule, fee, or country list.

The matched 2026-05-13 raw combined both full variants at the same canonical URL: own processor begins at old raw:10-26 and out-of-band at old raw:792-799. The 1,029-line diff replaces their combined body with variant links (diff:1-13,1026-1029). This is a collection/rendering shape change; old body omission does not deprecate either approach or establish that its behavior changed.

The dated source accurately distinguishes the May own-processor custom-payment-method plus PaymentRecord approach from the older out-of-band send_invoice/paid_out_of_band path (source:4-13,15-50), and its raw_files points to the full May evidence (source:6-7,78-80). Retain that factual raw link; the short November navigation page should not replace it as implementation evidence.

Own-processor May guidance has the merchant or platform collect through its third-party processor, while Stripe custom payment methods reference that instrument and PaymentRecords report the result; initial subscription is incomplete, with an open invoice, and the guide states a 23-hour reporting window (old raw:14-24,41-46,92-138,340). For renewals, invoice.payment_attempt_required, off-session collection, retry attempts against an existing record, and refund reporting with Credit Notes have distinct roles (old raw:342-346,433-443,548-555). These remain dated claims, not reconfirmed by the index.

The May out-of-band variant uses send_invoice with days_until_due, merchant-initiated third-party payment after invoice.finalized, and paid_out_of_band only after external success (old raw:859-899,955-979). It has different Checkout/Elements and customer-portal restrictions from the own-processor variant (old raw:32-40,609-616,823-825,901-903). The new index does not resolve these old variant-specific differences.

The source has a preexisting material typo: source:59 says customer portal proration_behavior=always_invoke, whereas old raw:38 says always_invoice; the concept correctly uses always_invoice (wiki/concepts/stripe-billing-third-party.md:45). Correct that scoped archival summary when next edited, without claiming a November API change. Source:13's 2026-04-22.dahlia appears in old Node examples (old raw:185,259,353), not as a universal prerequisite, and is not verified by the new index.
substantive_changes: No substantive payment-processing change is established by the same-URL new capture. It only changes the base page from a combined, two-variant full guide to an index of the own-processor and out-of-band variant URLs (new raw:9-14; diff:3-11,1028-1029).
historical_claims_to_preserve: Preserve May 2026 own-processor evidence as scoped: custom PaymentMethod and PaymentRecord with charge_automatically, separate external processor collection, account or customer identity, merchant legal/location responsibilities, no Stripe Checkout, no in-Stripe off-Stripe dispute/refund initiation, and limited recovery support (old raw:14-46,90-138,624-790). The new index alone cannot affirm present availability or supported country lists.

Preserve the May lifecycle distinctions: default_incomplete begins with open invoice; synchronous guaranteed/failed versus asynchronous initiated outcome; attachPayment/reporting and 23-hour incomplete_expired boundary; renewal invoice.payment_attempt_required; failed attempt leaves invoice open and can move a formerly active subscription to past_due (old raw:138,172-174,176-340,342-346,433-443). A reported/attached record is not a provider-side receipt in this review.

Preserve out-of-band as a distinct dated workflow: send_invoice and days_until_due, external payment, then paid_out_of_band; invoice email and portal settings affect unrelated users, and partial payments are unsupported in that guide (old raw:792-825,859-899,953-979,1025-1027). Do not transfer the own-processor Payment Element permission or retry automations into that path.
Preserve old source and concept routes as May evidence, with example API train 2026-04-22.dahlia labeled as an example rather than a cross-account requirement (source:13; old raw:185,259).
conflicts: Source:59 spells the customer-portal setting always_invoke, but old raw:38 and wiki/concepts/stripe-billing-third-party.md:45 spell always_invoice. The false token should receive a scoped correction in the source; this is an old-summary error, not an observed November product delta.

Own-processor old raw:32-40 permits Payment Element or a custom non-Stripe checkout flow but excludes Stripe Checkout; out-of-band old raw:901-903 excludes Checkout and Elements and calls for a custom checkout. Keep the variant scope explicit rather than deriving a universal Elements prohibition or permission from the two-label index.

Source:13 presents 2026-04-22.dahlia as an API version for the whole guide, but old raw:185,259,353 shows it in illustrative PaymentRecord Node code and old raw:324 even contains a malformed semicolon in one version string. No universal minimum or current account capability is established by those examples or by new raw:9-14.

Old raw:340 says attaching a PaymentRecord marks invoice paid/Subscription active, while old raw:252-317 describes an initiated asynchronous record and later outcome reporting. Treat payment initiation, reported guaranteed/failed outcome, invoice state, and actual third-party settlement as separate; the index cannot resolve that timing ambiguity.
unresolved_questions: What do the two query-parameter variant pages actually state on 2026-11-07 about PaymentRecords, supported processors and countries, Payment Element, invoices, retries, refunds, and out-of-band processing? They were not captured in this assigned new raw.

Do currently deployed account/API settings accept the historical own-processor and out-of-band flows? The capture contains no execution, entitlement, live processor result, or current country verification.

For asynchronous initiated PaymentRecords, at exactly what reported outcome and attachment step does the relevant invoice or subscription become paid/active? The May combined guide is internally ambiguous at old raw:252-340.

answers.Q1: For https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/third-party-payment-processing, the complete November capture establishes only two navigation routes, own processor and out-of-band invoices (new raw:9-14); it states no current prerequisites, API behavior, customer/account identities, or payment-status transitions. The matched May guide documented custom PaymentMethods plus PaymentRecords for charge_automatically subscriptions (old raw:14-19,41-46), with Customer v1 versus Account v2 examples, an incomplete first invoice and a stated 23-hour reporting window (old raw:90-138,340). Its separate out-of-band path used send_invoice, days_until_due, and paid_out_of_band after external success (old raw:792-799,859-899,965-979). [[source-stripe-subscriptions-third-party]] summarizes that dated full guide; the new index does not verify its implementation claims today.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/third-party-payment-processing, the observed change is navigation/rendering of two variant links (new raw:9-14; diff:3-11,1028-1029), not proof of a payment feature's removal or modification. Keep [[source-stripe-subscriptions-third-party]] and its May raw as dated evidence for variant-specific client/server work, Account v2 versus Customer v1, 23-hour and retry states, external processor responsibility, and out-of-band invoice marking (old raw:32-46,90-138,340,433-443,859-899,965-979). The source's always_invoke token conflicts with old raw:38's always_invoice, and the old own-processor Payment Element allowance differs from the out-of-band Elements restriction (old raw:32-40,901-903); both need scoped corrections or warnings. The 2026-04-22.dahlia sample code is not a demonstrated universal prerequisite, and an initiated or reported payment record is not independent proof of third-party settlement.
